intro: São Paulo rewards visitors with world-class museums, buzzing neighbourhoods and a food scene that never stops. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metrô and CPTM trains are modern, safe and the fastest way around; Lines 1-5 and 9 suit tourists.
Buses cover the whole city; fares are R$5.30 and Bilhete Único gives free transfers within 3 hours.
Taxis are metered; Guarucoop has a monopoly at GRU and fares are posted on a tabela.
Uber and 99 operate widely and are usually cheaper than taxis.
Driving is stressful; traffic peaks 06:00-09:00 and 16:00-19:00, so avoid renting a car.
Bikes are popular with many cycleways; walking is fine in central and Jardins areas.

ibirapuera.name: Ibirapuera Park
ibirapuera.price_text: Free entry · some museums inside charge separately
ibirapuera.hours: Park roughly 05:00–24:00 daily; museums have shorter hours — check on the day
ibirapuera.tip: Rent a bike or walk the lake loop early on Sunday, when avenues close to cars and the park fills with locals.

masp.name: São Paulo Museum of Art (MASP)
masp.price_text: Around BRL 75 · free on Tuesdays — confirm current price
masp.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–18:00, Thu until 20:00 · closed Monday
masp.tip: The famous red staircase and the free-standing paintings on glass easels are the highlight; go Tuesday for free entry.

paulista.name: Paulista Avenue
paulista.hours: Always open · closed to cars on Sundays
paulista.tip: Walk it on a Sunday when the avenue becomes a pedestrian street, and duck into the free cultural centres along the way.

mercado.name: Mercado Municipal de São Paulo
mercado.hours: Mon–Sat roughly 06:00–18:00, Sun until about 16:00 — check on the day
mercado.tip: Try a mortadella sandwich and pastel de bacalhau, but arrive before 11:00 to beat the crowds.

cathedral.name: São Paulo Cathedral (Catedral da Sé)
cathedral.hours: Roughly Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00, weekends shorter — check on the day
cathedral.tip: Visit in daylight and keep valuables out of sight in the surrounding square.

theatro.name: Theatro Municipal
theatro.price_text: Guided tour around BRL 20 · performances priced separately
theatro.hours: Guided tours on set days — check the schedule on the day
theatro.tip: Book a guided tour to see the ornate interior; evening concerts are a cheap way to experience it.

liberdade.name: Liberdade
liberdade.price_text: Free to walk · food paid separately
liberdade.tip: Come on a weekend for the street food stalls and Japanese-Brazilian snacks; the lantern-lit streets are best after dark.

batman.name: Batman Alley (Beco do Batman)
batman.tip: The murals change often, so wander the side streets too, then grab a coffee in Vila Madalena.

allianz.name: Allianz Parque
allianz.price_text: Match and concert tickets vary — check on the day
allianz.tip: Check the fixture list before you go; match nights are loud and fun but taxis are scarce afterwards.

altino.name: Altino Arantes Building (Farol Santander)
altino.price_text: Observation deck around BRL 40 — confirm on the day
altino.tip: The top-floor lookout gives one of the best free-ish views over Centro; go late afternoon for sunset light.

crianca.name: Cidade da Criança
crianca.price_text: Free entry — check on the day
crianca.hours: Daytime hours only — check on the day
crianca.tip: A small family-friendly park inside Ibirapuera; good for a break with kids mid-walk.

copan.name: Copan Building
copan.tip: Admire the Oscar Niemeyer curve from the street; the interior is residential, so don't wander in.

morumbi.name: Estádio do Morumbi
morumbi.price_text: Match tickets vary — check on the day
morumbi.hours: Only open for events and tours
morumbi.tip: It's far from the centre; go only if you have a match ticket and plan transport back in advance.

bandeiras.name: Monument to the Bandeiras
bandeiras.tip: It sits at the Ibirapuera entrance, so see it on the way into the park.

octavio.name: Octavio Frias de Oliveira Bridge
octavio.tip: See it lit up after dark from a nearby riverside spot; it's a quick photo stop, not a long visit.

marisa.name: Parque Marisa
marisa.hours: Daytime hours — check on the day
marisa.tip: A small local park; pair it with a walk in nearby Vila Madalena rather than a special trip.

pinacoteca.name: Pinacoteca do Estado
pinacoteca.price_text: Around BRL 30 · free on Saturdays — confirm on the day
pinacoteca.tip: Brazilian art in a beautiful old building; Saturdays are free and busy, so go early.

playcenter.name: Playcenter Family
playcenter.price_text: Ticket prices vary — check on the day
playcenter.hours: Check opening days on the day
playcenter.tip: An indoor family amusement option; confirm hours and prices online before travelling.

zoo.name: São Paulo Zoo
zoo.price_text: Around BRL 65 — confirm on the day
zoo.tip: It's large and far south; go early, wear comfortable shoes and bring water.

farol.name: Farol Santander viewpoint
farol.price_text: Around BRL 40 — confirm on the day
farol.tip: A rooftop lookout over Centro; check visibility on the day before buying a ticket.

vila-madalena-walk.name: Vila Madalena neighbourhood walk
vila-madalena-walk.price_text: Free to walk · food and drink paid separately
vila-madalena-walk.tip: Wander the streets between Batman Alley and the bars; evenings are lively but keep to busy streets.

liberdade-food-tour.name: Liberdade street food walk
liberdade-food-tour.price_text: Pay per stall — budget around BRL 50–100
liberdade-food-tour.tip: Bring cash for small stalls and try a few snacks rather than one big meal.

centro-walk.name: Centro histórico walking tour
centro-walk.price_text: Free walking tours tip-based — check on the day
centro-walk.hours: Tours usually run mornings and afternoons
centro-walk.tip: Join a guided group rather than exploring alone; it's the easiest way to see the old centre safely.

jardins-food.name: Jardins restaurant and café stroll
jardins-food.hours: Cafés daytime · restaurants into the evening
jardins-food.tip: Walk the tree-lined streets around Oscar Freire for cafés and shops; book dinner on weekends.

sunday-avenue.name: Sunday car-free Paulista bike ride
sunday-avenue.tip: Rent a bike on Sunday when the avenue closes to cars, and ride the car-free stretch at an easy pace.

stays.why: Leafy, safe and central. Walk to Avenida Paulista and the MASP; good restaurants nearby.
Right on the main avenue and metro line. Best base for first-time sightseeing.
Street art, bars and nightlife. Livelier and a bit rougher; use ride apps at night.
Cheapest and closest to historic sights and markets. Busy by day, quiet after dark; check the block.

food: Try a Brazilian lunch: feijoada (bean and pork stew) or a prato feito (rice, beans, meat and salad), often R$30–60.
Mercado Municipal downtown: pastel de bacalhau and huge mortadella sandwiches. Go before noon to beat the crowds.
Padarias (bakeries) serve cheap breakfasts and coffee all day; a pão na chapa and coffee is about R$10–15.
São Paulo has strong Japanese, Italian and Arab food. Look for restaurants in Liberdade and Bixiga.
Churrascarias and kilo buffets (comida por kilo) are good value; pay by weight, usually R$60–100 per kilo.
more_time: Add a day for Ibirapuera Park and the museums around it; it is a big park and easy to spend half a day.
Swap one city day for a trip to the coast or the hills; check bus times and prices on the day.
Art lovers can swap a shopping afternoon for the Pinacoteca and the Luz area near the Centro.
